Do not reject matching using project completion alone—but do not keep it on that explanation without measuring preparation burden and observing a paid choice.

uncertainty: Commuters prefer ninety-second narrated discovery to reading the underlying listing or their existing commute routine.

Proposed kill test, not run: invite ten consenting SSE commuters, offer three independently checked episodes within seven days, cap cash at €20 and total team work at six hours. Require four of ten to voluntarily play a different episode without individual reminders or repeat-play rewards; missing c

If that screen passes, counterbalance matched audio and listing offers; require at least six of ten to choose audio for their next commute and explain a specific benefit. Failure rejects the claimed audio advantage, not culture discovery generally.

An initial pass may be novelty. Before adopting daily production, propose a second-week retention screen requiring at least four of the original ten to voluntarily return again, with no individual reminders and production time recorded.
A future listener subscription or sponsor could cover recurring human work, but free repeat listening would not establish either payer.
dissent: Four repeat listeners among ten personally recruited students could reflect goodwill; teammate or mentor agreement adds no independent evidence.
A failed tiny pilot cannot rule out every audience or weekly format. It can justify stopping this daily commuter proposition under its stated constraints.
A worthwhile free cultural project need not become profitable, but it still needs an explicit subsidy and sustainable human-time budget.
